preamble: Insertion of a rhotic to break vowel hiatus at word or morpheme boundaries. The best-known case is intrusive r in non-rhotic English, where the inserted sound is the approximant [ɹ] (filed here under r, since the atlas has no separate ɹ symbol). Central Bavarian German shows a parallel sandhi rule in which r (or n) is inserted as a hiatus breaker.

examples.note: No r in the spelling or etymology; [ɹ] is inserted after a non-high final vowel before a vowel
Word-internal intrusive [ɹ] at a morpheme boundary
r inserted between two vowels across a morpheme boundary as a hiatus breaker
Final n of gegen is lost in the dialect; r, not the etymological n, fills the hiatus
